# General Design System (GDS)

> GDS is a governed, cross-project React design system published as `@sovereignsquad/gds`. It is built on Mantine and ships 324 components, design tokens, theme presets, and runtime systems (forms, tables, overlays, notifications, access gates, i18n). Every product surface is composed from shipped GDS contracts — never reinvented locally.

This file is the entry point for AI coding agents (any LLM-powered coding tool). It tells you what GDS is, how to install it, the non-negotiable rules, and where to read more. When building UI for a project that uses GDS, follow these rules and compose the shipped components — do not author parallel primitives or raw CSS.

## Install

GDS publishes exclusively to GitHub Packages' npm-compatible registry (`https://npm.pkg.github.com`) — there is no npmjs.com publish and no anonymous install, even for public packages. Add this to `.npmrc` first:

```ini
@sovereignsquad:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com
//npm.pkg.github.com/:_authToken=${GITHUB_TOKEN}
```

`GITHUB_TOKEN` is a personal access token with `read:packages` scope (yours, or your CI's provisioned token) — not a GDS-owned secret. Then:

```bash
npm install @sovereignsquad/gds react react-dom
```

npm 7+ installs the umbrella's `peerDependencies` automatically. When peer auto-install is off (for example `--legacy-peer-deps`), follow the peer-dependency rule in INSTALLATION_GUIDE.md "Single install surface".

Bootstrap is two steps. Both are required; neither replaces the other.

1. Load the GDS stylesheet exactly once at the app entry, before any app styles:

```tsx
import '@sovereignsquad/gds-theme/styles.css';
```

2. Wrap the app once in `GdsProvider`, then compose components:

```tsx
import { GdsProvider, MetricCard, SemanticButton } from '@sovereignsquad/gds';

export default function App() {
  return (
    <GdsProvider defaultColorScheme="light">
      <MetricCard label="Active adopters" value="18 apps" trend={{ tone: 'positive', label: '+2%' }} />
      <SemanticButton action="save" />
    </GdsProvider>
  );
}
```

What each step supplies:

- The stylesheet: the Mantine component CSS (it already includes `@mantine/core/styles.css` and `@mantine/notifications/styles.css`, so do not import those separately), the default `--gds-*` role, overlay and motion tokens, the Inter font, the rules gated on `data-gds-theme-preset`, and the `forced-colors`, `prefers-reduced-motion` and global `:focus-visible` rules.
- `GdsProvider`: the Mantine theme (`gdsTheme` unless you pass `theme`) and its `--mantine-*` variables, color-scheme handling, text direction, locale and messages, and the modals and notifications mounts. It writes `--gds-*` variables only when the theme carries `theme.other.gdsCssVariables` (themes built with `createBrandTheme`), and it loads no fonts. Without it, Mantine-backed components throw.

Never add a second provider or a second Mantine `MantineProvider`. `GdsProvider` is also the only color-scheme authority: add no scheme library (such as `next-themes`), no `html` class toggle and no `color-scheme` declaration in app CSS. Single-scheme, OS-following and user-switchable recipes: THEME_GOVERNANCE.md "Colour scheme".

## Non-negotiable rules for agents

- Compose shipped GDS components first. Do not import `@mantine/core` directly: the Mantine components GDS re-exports (the list in `packages/gds-core/src/GdsPrimitives.tsx`) are imported from `@sovereignsquad/gds` or `@sovereignsquad/gds/client`, and the policy plus the GDS replacement for each Mantine name GDS does not re-export are in DEPENDENCY_GOVERNANCE.md "Mantine boundary". Do not build ad-hoc HTML/CSS controls where a GDS contract exists.
- Style with component props and theme tokens, not custom CSS classes or raw hex, rgb, px, rem or bare numbers (`gap={48}`, `maw={860}`). Use GDS layout primitives (`GdsStack`, `GdsInline`, `GdsBox`, `GdsGrid`) with their token props (`gap`, `padding`, `margin`, `maxWidth`), and Mantine props (`c`, `bg`, `mt`, `size`, `variant`, `color`, `radius`) on the components whose props include them. Mantine spacing props resolve only the `gdsTheme.spacing` keys (`xs`–`xl`); layout primitives also accept `2xl`. Steps per prop family, and the values that have no step: docs/SAFE_STYLING.md.
- `SemanticButton` (and `ActionBar`, `SemanticNavLink`, page/template actions) take a semantic `action` enum (`save`, `add`, `edit`, `delete`, `search`, `settings`, `export`, `refresh`, `submit`, …), not free text. Use `add` (not "create") and `refresh` (not "retry").
- `Select` and `MultiSelect` are Mantine passthroughs (import from `@sovereignsquad/gds/client`); they and `AdminSelect` take a `data={[{value,label}]}` prop, not `<option>` children. `SearchableSelect` (typeahead, async options) takes `options` instead. Prefer `AdminSelect` in admin forms and `SearchableSelect` for searchable or async lists.
- Every interactive surface designs loading / empty / error / disabled / success states — use `StateBlock`, `EmptyState`, and the `loading`/`error` props components expose.
- Access-gated content uses `GdsAccessGate` with `protectedContentPolicy="never-render-while-locked"` so private/paid content is never mounted while locked.
- Accessibility (visible focus, AA contrast, semantic labels, focus traps) and responsive/localized layout are acceptance criteria, not cleanup.
- One element that must keep its own explicit styling under a theme preset (a brand-coloured `Paper`, an outline `Button`, a `Popover.Dropdown`, an `AppShell` navbar) carries `data-gds-fixed-tone` — never a `!important` counter-rule against the preset stylesheet. Element-level, not inherited; see THEME_GOVERNANCE.md "Opting one element out of the preset repaint".

## Packages

- `@sovereignsquad/gds` — umbrella install (theme + core + admin); root, `/client`, `/server` entrypoints.
- `@sovereignsquad/gds-theme` — tokens, theme presets, VibeThemes, font lanes, motion system.
- `@sovereignsquad/gds-core` — layouts, cards, shells, forms, tables, overlays, charts, access, i18n.
- `@sovereignsquad/gds-admin` — operator scaffolds (`AppShell`, `PageHeader`, `ContentOpsEditor`, `ResponsiveDataView`).
- `@sovereignsquad/gds-a11y` — Playwright/axe accessibility test helpers.
- `@sovereignsquad/gds-eslint-config`, `@sovereignsquad/gds-compliance` — shared lint + adoption enforcement.

## Component families

- Layout: `GdsBox`, `GdsStack`, `GdsInline`, `GdsCluster`, `GdsGrid`, `GdsColumnGrid`/`GdsColumnGridItem` (named 12-column track-span grid), `GdsSplit`, `GdsSidebar`, `GdsContainer`, `GdsBleed`
- Shells: `AppShell`, `PublicShell`, `AuthShell`, `ArticleShell`, `DiscoveryShell`, `WorkspaceHeader`, `PageHeader`, `GdsBreadcrumbs`
- Cards/surfaces: `MetricCard`, `ProgressCard`, `GdsMeter`, `ProductCard`, `PublicProductCard`, `EditorialCard`, `EditorialHero`, `InfoCard`, `SectionPanel`, `ReportingSection`, `AccentPanel`, `StatsStrip`
- Component selection (full rules: COMPONENTS_AND_PATTERNS.md "Component Selection Rules"):
  - `SectionPanel` — the titled panel for dashboards, detail pages and settings groups. `tone="warning"`/`"critical"` sets only the background, so the title states the severity.
  - `ReportingSection` — report data only (period, metrics, chart, table and evidence slots; report-worded state copy). Use `SectionPanel`, not `ReportingSection`, when there are no period controls, metrics, charting, table fallback or evidence; settings pages use `GdsSettingsTemplate`.
  - `AccentPanel` — `tone` is a decorative color family with no severity meaning, and the panel has no `role`. Severity goes to `InlineAlert` or `BannerNotice` `severity`, with the severity also stated in text.
  - `PublicProductCard` — retail only: it always renders an availability badge (`state` defaults to `'available'`) and labels its helper rows "Pickup" and "Availability". Courses and other progress-bearing items use `ListingCard`; GDS has no progress slot on a listing card.
  - `MetricCard` — one numeric KPI (a count, amount, ratio or duration) and its trend. Not for identifiers, addresses, selections, categorical labels or `-` placeholders; label/value text goes to `DetailFactsTable`.
  - `ProgressCard` — an operation in flight (`role="progressbar"`). A static measurement is a `GdsMeter`.
  - `GdsMeter` — a static measurement within a known range (score, completion %, quota usage) with `role="meter"`; not a progress bar.
- Forms: `GdsForm`, `GdsSchemaForm` (schema-driven; field types include `checkbox-group` grouped multi-select and `repeatable` "add another row of N fields", alongside text/select/date/file-upload/…), `FormField`, `FormSection`, `SearchableSelect`, Mantine passthroughs `Select`, `MultiSelect`, `TextInput`, `Switch`, `Radio` (import from `@sovereignsquad/gds/client`), `GdsDateInput`, `GdsDateTimeInput`, `GdsDateRangeInput` (date components need the opt-in `@sovereignsquad/gds-theme/dates.css` import + `@mantine/dates`/`dayjs`), `GdsRichTextEditor` (import from `@sovereignsquad/gds-core/rich-text-editor`, not the main entry — its Tiptap dependency is deliberately opt-in)
- Data: `GdsDataTable`/`DataTable` (via `createGdsTableAdapter`), `SimpleDataTable`, `Table` (Mantine passthrough, import from `@sovereignsquad/gds/client`), `GdsBarChart`, `GdsLineChart`
- Feedback/overlay: `EmptyState`, `StateBlock`, `GdsNotificationProvider`+`GdsNotificationCenter`, `GdsModal`, `GdsDrawer`, `ConfirmDialog`, `CommandPalette`
- Operations: `KanbanBoard` (stage/column tracking — portrait-mobile stacked, landscape/tablet/desktop multi-column; keyboard-accessible move-to-column menu always available, plus an opt-in `enableDrag` pointer/touch/keyboard drag handle built on `@dnd-kit`, never native HTML5 drag-and-drop; generic over item/column shape — `KanbanBoard<TItem, TColumn>` — for typed `renderItem` on app-extended records, defaulting to the base contracts. Columns support `totalCount` (server-paginated count badge), a `ReactNode` `title` (+`ariaLabel`), a `footer`/`renderColumnFooter` slot, and opt-in `collapsible` columns with board-level `collapsedColumnIds`/`onCollapsedChange`.)
- Access: `GdsAccessGate`, `AccessSummary`, `AccessRecoveryPanel`, social/provider auth buttons
- Overlays & onboarding: `GdsModal`/`GdsDrawer`/`GdsSheet` + `OverlayManagerProvider`; `GdsTourProvider` / `useGdsTour` / `GdsGuidedTour` (guided onboarding tour — spotlight coach-marks that dim the page and highlight one function at a time; targets via `data-gds-tour-target`; focus-trapped, keyboard + forced-colors + i18n governed)
- Creator-authored styling and consent: `CreatorThemeBoundary` wraps its children in a `data-gds-creator-theme` scope and injects creator CSS only when `validateCreatorCss` reports no error; otherwise it renders `CreatorThemeDiagnostics`. The validator checks no contrast and does not evaluate `requiredVisibleSelectors`, so consent, legal and recovery controls render outside the creator canvas. `PublicConsentStep` lays out consent copy above a control you supply; GDS has no cookie-consent banner, accept-state persistence or CTA-gating primitive. Creator, tenant and admin-authored styling rules: THEME_GOVERNANCE.md "Creator-authored experience theming" and "White-label and tenant theming".
